result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_periphery()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get periphery nodes (nodes with maximum eccentricity). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L25022-L25063){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_periphery() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Periphery](/assets/graphs/get-periphery.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A six-node graph with each node's eccentricity in a badge. The end nodes A and F have the maximum eccentricity 4 and are drawn in the accent color. The card returns their node ids, 1 and 6." width="100%"} Periphery nodes are farthest from the graph's center. These nodes have the maximum eccentricity (longest shortest path to any other node). Returns empty list if graph is disconnected. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of node IDs in the periphery, empty if disconnected. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The periphery is the set of nodes attaining the graph's diameter, that is those with $\mathrm{ecc}(v) = \max_u \mathrm{ecc}(u)$. It is the natural dual of the graph's *center* (minimum-eccentricity nodes) and reveals which parts of the network sit furthest from everything else. On a tree it always consists of leaves. Multiple nodes commonly tie for maximum eccentricity; all such nodes are returned. If the graph is disconnected, eccentricity is undefined across components and the method returns an empty list rather than picking a single component. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a path graph `1-2-3-4-5`, the two endpoints are farthest from the graph's center, so they form the periphery: ::: {#dcc7ef5b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(5) periphery_ids = graph.get_periphery() # Returns 2 (the two endpoints) len(periphery_ids) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
